tldr: AgentFactory keeps successful task solutions as executable Python subagents — not textual reflections — in a growing library, refines them from execution feedback, and re-exports them to other agent systems; saved subagents cut orchestrator output tokens roughly in half on transfer tasks.
method: A Meta-Agent orchestrates a three-tier skill system: fixed meta-skills (create_subagent, run_subagent, modify_subagent, list_saved_subagents, view_subagent_code, finish), fixed tool skills (Serper web_search, Jina web_reading, Playwright browser_automation, shell_command), and the one evolving tier — subagent skills saved as pure Python code plus a SKILL.md doc. Install: on an unsolved task the Meta-Agent decomposes it and builds a focused Python subagent per sub-problem, allocating each a tool subset rather than the whole toolset; on success the subagent is promoted from the isolated per-task workspace to the persistent library. Self-Evolve: on similar tasks it retrieves saved subagents, runs and assesses them, analyzes failure feedback, modifies the code (error handling, generality), and revalidates against the current task. Deploy: mature subagents export as standalone scripts; LangChain, AutoGen, and Claude Code onboard them via prompts + SKILL.md alone.
results: Table 1, Batch 2 transfer tasks with saved subagents, avg orchestrator output tokens/task: Opus 4.6 2971 vs ReAct 7022 (−58%) and 6210 for the textual-experience baseline; Sonnet 4.6 3862 vs ReAct 7029 (−45%) and 8223 textual

Stronger models reuse even without a pre-built library: Opus 4.6 already drops to 4324 tokens on Batch 1 from scratch vs ReAct 8298 (the paper flags this as a signal for future models); Sonnet 4.6 does not — 9199 vs ReAct 6893, i.e. building subagents from scratch cost more than plain ReAct

The metric isolates orchestration effort (subagent-internal LLM tokens excluded); setup is two 15-task batches where each Batch 2 task mirrors its Batch 1 counterpart with changed specifics, and all tasks completed without runtime errors in every configuration

Qualitative loops: a README-generation subagent evolves hardcoded path → LLM JSON parsing with fragile hardcoded fallback → LLM + regex fallback over three runs (Fig. 2); subagents created in AgentFactory (Audio Transcriber, Document Creator) are invoked directly inside Claude Code with no new subagent creation (Fig. 3)
advantages: Experience is executable: saved subagents re-run as code, so reuse replaces re-derivation — the Reflexion/STaR-style textual-experience baseline never approaches the Batch 2 savings (6210/8223 vs 2971/3862 tokens)
Cross-system portability is demonstrated, not just claimed: pure-Python subagents with SKILL.md docs (aligned to Anthropic's Agent Skills standard) onboarded into Claude Code via prompts alone

Improvement by accumulation under containment: meta- and tool-skills stay frozen while only the subagent tier evolves, and the Workspace Manager runs each task in isolation so failed modifications can't corrupt the shared library
limitations: The headline metric excludes subagent-internal token consumption — savings are orchestration-level only, and there is no output-quality score beyond 'all tasks completed without runtime errors' on 30 author-curated tasks
The from-scratch overhead is backbone-dependent: Sonnet 4.6's Batch 1 orchestration cost (9199) exceeds ReAct (6893); the paper's text highlights only the favorable Opus contrast (4324 vs 8298)
Interaction is web-only (search, reading, Playwright); the conclusion defers GUI/non-web applications to future VLM integration

Safety is by convention rather than guarantee: shell_command has built-in checks that flag destructive operations, and the ethical considerations section relies on human-readable code plus user auditing of exported subagents
fits: Stage 5 harness-level RSI (Self-Evolving Agent Frameworks): Voyager's code-as-skill lifted from single functions to whole subagents, with the paper's own ablation being Reflexion/STaR textual experience. Pairs with DGM (evolves the agent's internals rather than growing a capability library) and the stage-10 AgentFactory repo card for the implementation.
